problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $3{x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{3}$ is the third component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Components of a Vector with Respect to an Orthogonal or Orthonormal Basis

feedback.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]}$  of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{4}{\sqrt{13}}-\frac{21}{\sqrt{13}}=-\frac{25}{\sqrt{13}} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{6}{\sqrt{13}}+\frac{14}{\sqrt{13}}=\frac{8}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{25}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{8}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}].
$$
